😳 The world's most expensive employee doesn't work for Goldman Sachs or Citadel — he works for Claude

According to Axios, one company forgot to set usage limits for Claude AI.

The result? Employees burned through $500 million worth of tokens in a single month. 🙀

Remember when startups said, "We'll replace workers with AI to cut costs"?

Turns out the new strategy is:

❌ Claude tokens: $500,000,000/month
✅ Sleep-deprived employee: $3900/month

For the first time in years, being underpaid might actually be a competitive advantage. 🤝

🎲 A controversial ruling on Polymarket has sparked outrage after a market with more than $20 million in volume asked: “Will Strategy sell Bitcoin before May 31?”

Despite evidence that Strategy sold 32 BTC between May 26–31, Polymarket resolved the market as "NO", arguing that confirmation of the sale became public only after the market had closed. 🥴

One trader reportedly accumulated 200,000 “YES” shares for around $15,000, seeing unrealized profits climb to $150,000 before the disputed outcome wiped them out.

🔎 Critics argue the market’s rules focused on whether Strategy sold BTC before May 31—not when the sale was disclosed. Even Grok weighed in, stating that Strategy’s June 1 filing confirmed the sale occurred within the required timeframe and that the resolution should therefore be “YES.”

The dispute has reignited concerns about oracle decisions, market integrity, and trust in prediction platforms. 😤

💰 A rare Casascius physical Bitcoin containing 25 BTC has finally been redeemed after sitting untouched for 12 years

When the coin was created in the early 2010s, the BTC stored inside was worth less than $100. Today, those same 25 BTC are valued at roughly $1.8 million.

🔎 The owner recently peeled off the security hologram and moved the coins to a new wallet for the first time. But there was a tradeoff: by opening the coin, they permanently destroyed much of its collector value.

Unredeemed Casascius coins are highly sought-after Bitcoin artifacts, often selling for tens of thousands of dollars above the value of the BTC they contain. Once opened, that collectible premium largely disappears. 🤷

The move has sparked speculation that the owner may be preparing to sell. After holding through more than a decade of volatility, choosing to cash out during a market correction seems unusual—but sometimes liquidity needs outweigh perfect timing. 👀
